title: bug(plugin-kanban): the swimlane header row's horizontal scroll range is 10px SHORTER than the lane rows' — at the right end of the axis every title sits 9px off its column
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8449 (the vertical arm). ⛔ Not claimed, not graded — priority and routing labels are the triage seat's.

## What is wrong

objectui#8448 gave the swimlane board ONE horizontal axis: a scroll handler copies `scrollLeft` from whichever row the user drove onto the header row and every other lane row. That works everywhere except at the RIGHT END of the range, because the two kinds of row do not have the same range:

- the header row is `flex shrink-0 gap-3 sm:gap-4 pl-36 sm:pl-44 ... overflow-x-auto`
- each lane content row is `flex gap-3 sm:gap-4 overflow-x-auto px-2 pb-3 pl-36 sm:pl-44`

The lane rows carry `px-2` that the header row does not, so their scrollable width is larger. The sync assigns the lane's `scrollLeft` to the header row, the header row CLAMPS it to its own smaller maximum, and from that point on the titles stop tracking their columns.

## Measured

Chromium 1194 at 1600x1000, real Tailwind CSS, five columns and six swimlanes, driving one lane row and reading every row plus the worst distance between a column title's centre and its own lane cell's centre:

```
header row max scrollLeft : 288
lane row   max scrollLeft : 298

asked scrollLeft   rows land at                      worst title/cell dx
     0             [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]                    1px
   100             [100,100,100,100,100,100,100]      1px
   200             [200,200,200,200,200,200,200]      1px
   288             [288,288,288,288,288,288,288]      1px
   298             [288,298,298,298,298,298,298]      9px
  1000             [288,298,298,298,298,298,298]      9px
```

⇒ scroll the board fully to the right and every column title sits 9px off its own column, permanently, until you scroll back. The 10px shortfall is exactly the header row's missing horizontal padding.

## Why this is not objectui#8448 and not objectui#8449

- objectui#8448 was that the rows were INDEPENDENT scroll containers — a lane driven to 298 left the header at 0, a 297px error. That is fixed and stays fixed; this is the residue at the end of the range, and objectui#8448's pin asserts propagation (`scrollLeft` equality after a `fireEvent.scroll`), which cannot see a clamp that happens only past the header row's own maximum.
- objectui#8449 is the vertical axis and does not touch this. The numbers above are identical before and after that change.

Same defect FAMILY as objectui#8448 — the board says a column is somewhere it is not — but a different cause and a different fix (the two rows need the same horizontal padding, or the sync needs to scale rather than copy). Deciding which is a layout call, not a mechanical one.

## Severity

Bounded and cosmetic-adjacent: 9px, only at the extreme right of the axis, and it is 1px everywhere else. It is filed because it is measured and reproducible, not because it is urgent.

## Dedup

Run, and it returned a LIT reading rather than a zero: a targeted `search_issues` for the swimlane header row's scroll range returned objectui#8449, objectui#8448, objectui#7303 and objectui#8508 — every adjacent card — and none of them is this defect. Note that a zero from this channel in this repo has previously been a false zero, which is why a positive control is quoted rather than an absence.
